sentences.text: Advertising, politics, and social media all spend enormous effort on appearances.
Some people argue that in contemporary society, creating an appealing image has become more important than the truth behind it.
I agree that image often seems to dominate today, but I believe truth still matters deeply in the end.
First, it is true that image frequently seems to matter more than reality today.
People and companies often spend more on looking good than on actually being good.
For example, a product with clever advertising can outsell a better but less glamorous rival.
This shows that a polished image can shape opinions more powerfully than the plain truth.
Politicians, too, are sometimes judged by their style rather than their actual record.
In a world of fast media, a striking image can spread before the truth is even known.
To this extent, the statement captures a real feature of modern life.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why truth still reasserts itself

sentences.text: Second, however, the truth behind an image still matters and usually reasserts itself.
A false image may impress people briefly, but reality eventually breaks through.
Consider a company that sells a poor product through clever marketing and quickly loses its customers.
Such failures show that image alone cannot survive once the truth becomes clear.
Lies and empty appearances tend to collapse the moment they are tested against the facts.
Lasting trust and success, in the end, depend on substance rather than mere appearance.
Truth, then, remains more powerful than image over the long run.
In conclusion, creating an appealing image does carry great weight in today's society.
But truth still matters deeply, since false images rarely survive close examination.
Image may win the moment, yet in the long run it is the truth that endures.
